frequency_question: How frequently has Congress successfully blocked a submitted nuclear cooperation agreement via a joint resolution of disapproval within the statutory review window?
membership_rule: Includes any peaceful nuclear cooperation agreement (Section 123 agreement) formally submitted by the executive branch to Congress for the mandatory review period of 90 continuous session days. Excludes informal negotiations or agreements not formally submitted.

cases.name: Agreement for Cooperation Concerning Civil Uses of Atomic Energy (Various historical submissions)

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 1 named (30.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 30+ named historical submissions; exactly 0 successful legislative blocks that survived presidential veto or were enacted over veto.
known_gaps: While non-binding resolutions or attempted disapprovals have occurred (e.g., regarding the Middle East in recent years), zero joint resolutions of disapproval have ever successfully become law to block a 123 agreement.
skeleton: Total formal 123 agreements submitted to Congress historically (approx. 30+ major agreements) multiplied by the historical rate of successful statutory blocking via joint resolution of disapproval.
multiplier: 30 agreements * 0% historical passage rate resulting in a successful block
validity_reason: The statutory framework under the Atomic Energy Act for congressional review of 123 agreements remains stable across decades, changing only via major legislative overhauls.
